title: Swiggy Ltd - 544285 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Swiggy Q2 FY27: Quick commerce NOV grew 13.4% QoQ with 1.3 million MTUs added, while Toing investment stays range-bound and food margin target of 5% of GOV is reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Management reported a return to growth in quick commerce, with NOV up 13.4% QoQ, 1.3 million MTUs added, and orders per dark store per day up about 9% sequentially to close to 1,200. Food delivery guidance of 18-20% YoY growth on the standalone business was reiterated, with Adjusted EBITDA up about INR 50 crore for the quarter and take rate above 26%. Toing, the affordability platform, is being run as a range-bound investment; management asked for another quarter or two before judging whether it is a scalable model. Quick commerce contribution margin guidance is 0 to -100 bps, with 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement guided for Q3, and a move to an inventory model starting mid-quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Return to growth after a reset quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Quick commerce orders per day per store

financial_highlights.value: close to INR 50 crore added in the quarter
About INR 4 billion loss, INR 5 billion revenue (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: Food Marketplace (Swiggy core food delivery)
segments.commentary: Management expects 18-20% YoY standalone growth, with Swiggy back above 20% growth in September 2026. Take rate exceeded 26% and Adjusted EBITDA rose about INR 50 crore; the 5% of GOV margin target is still intended to be reached sequentially.

segments.name: Toing (affordability food platform)
segments.commentary: Four quarters old and run as range-bound investment. About 2 in 3 users are new to the platform, dual-app users show 25% higher orders per user, and retention is better than the core app. 70-80% of users are under 30 years old.

segments.name: Instamart (quick commerce)
segments.commentary: NOV grew 13.4% QoQ with 1.3 million MTUs added. Contribution margin guided to 0 to -100 bps, with sequential improvement; differentiated assortment (Noice, Nectar) is about 20% of orders, with Noice at 1 in 8 orders.

guidance_outlook: Food delivery standalone growth guided at 18-20% YoY for FY27, with 5% of GOV Adjusted EBITDA margin trajectory to be reached sequentially; no pricing action or dilutive route expected near term.
Toing growth ambition raised to 25-30% for overall food marketplace from 18-20%; management says it is closer to the lower end of that range and investment will stay range-bound.
Quick commerce: double-digit sequential NOV growth guided for Q3 FY27, with contribution margin in a 0 to -100 bps range and 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement guided for the current quarter.
Move to inventory model to start mid-quarter (Q3) and fully transition over the next two to three quarters; no benefit assumed in the 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA guidance.
Management says the next milestone is Adjusted EBITDA zero for the business, and that it needs to roughly double its current size.
capex_capacity: Store opening trigger is about 2,000 orders per day per store; new stores reach 2,300-2,500 orders per day after 2-3 months.
Roughly 5-7% of the store network reaches the capacity threshold each quarter, so store additions are a function of growth; the company expects to keep adding stores in Q3.
Present in 130+ cities with no near-term plan to expand geographic coverage; growth will come from densification within existing cities.
Megapod (large-format) and hyperlocal stores run together; management says no change in store configuration is planned.
demand_pricing: Competition: Rapido is live in food to the public; Flipkart Minutes has not opened at scale in Bangalore. Management says the competitive intensity remains high and expects no easing near term, though some easing was seen in some months.
Toing overlap with core Swiggy food is reducing as the platform scales, per management.
Quick commerce pricing intervention was cited by an analyst as lowering NOV-to-GOV ratio in the current quarter; management attributed growth to cohorts, retention and differentiated assortment.

Monetisation (commission, ads, consumer fees) has been flat for three quarters per an analyst; management says it is working with brands on co-created assortment and will evolve consumer fees over time.
Gross margin fell about 110-120 bps QoQ in quick commerce, per an analyst, linked to private label mix; management said 60 bps added in the previous quarter was partly reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How should losses in quick commerce evolve and will Swiggy refocus on Tier-2 markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quick commerce returned to growth with 13.4% QoQ NOV growth and 1.3 million MTUs added, and that it is not looking to expand geographically beyond its current footprint of around 130 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Is Toing an experiment or ready to scale, and what metrics decide this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked for another one to two quarters before deciding. Metrics are repeat-user unit economics in early cities, customer acquisition cost as the base expands, and delivery cost reduction; investment is discretionary and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the contribution margin trajectory in quick commerce improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 0 to -100 bps contribution margin with sequential improvement and 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement in Q3, with the inventory model contributing no benefit in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store capacity threshold for adding new dark stores?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores are triggered at about 2,000 orders per day, reach 2,300-2,500 within 2-3 months, and 5-7% of the network reaches capacity each quarter, so additions are an outcome of growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will food margins be sacrificed for growth as competition rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 5% of GOV margin path continues, with take rate above 26% and operating leverage. Reinvestment for growth would only be considered after 5%; no dilutive pricing action is needed in the core business.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the NOV per store gap with Blinkit persisted, and has competition eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said productivity will come from category mix and pod productivity, with no change to network configuration. On competition, it said some months showed easing but it is too early to call, with new players entering.

risks_watch: Toing losses and revenue trajectory: management says losses stay range-bound while revenue scales, but no breakeven timeline was given.
Competitive intensity in quick commerce and food, with Rapido live and Flipkart Minutes and other entrants expanding; festive-season timing distorts quarter-on-quarter comparisons.
Quick commerce gross margin pressure and monetisation stagnation, with the NOV-to-GOV ratio affected by pricing intervention.
Execution of the inventory model transition over two to three quarters and its effect on quick commerce margins.
Quick commerce NOV per store gap versus Blinkit (about 50%, per an analyst), which management did not quantify a plan to close beyond productivity and mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quick commerce growth rebound and food profitability, but cautious on Toing, where management repeatedly deferred scaling decisions by one to two quarters. Management was evasive on Q3 festive-season growth and on the NOV-per-store gap versus Blinkit.
key_quotes: We would be closer to that lower end of that range that we talk.
Right now, we won't comment as we are in the beginning of the quarter.
As we mentioned, we need to get to roughly 2x the current size.

adds.what: Quick commerce dark stores: additions tied to capacity maxing out (store trigger ~2,000 orders/day/store); ~5-7% of network hits threshold each quarter

growth.why: Management reiterates 18-20% YoY standalone food delivery growth for FY27 and double-digit sequential quick commerce NOV growth for Q3, backed by 13.4% QoQ NOV growth, ~9% QoQ orders per store gain and store additions where capacity is maxing out, though the backing is partly numeric and partly qualitative (no store count or capex given).
